summary: Jeff Shore is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as a professor at Hanazono University from around 1987 to 2023, becoming professor emeritus around 2023.
Jeff Watt is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under teacher Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Jeff Wilson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and was mentored by Taitetsu Unno (attested 2009) and postdoctoral mentor Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Notre Dame (BA) and the University of Chicago (MA, PhD), he became Associate Professor of Religion and Asian Studies at Elizabethtown College in 2000.

Jeffrey Broughton specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1975 and served as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University, Long Beach (attested 2004).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Missouri State University and UC Santa Barbara (PhD 2002 under David Gordon White). He held posts at Missouri State, UC Santa Barbara, and became Assistant Professor at Marshall University in 2002.

Jeffrey Davis Schoening specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), where he was advised by Sanghasen Singh and supervised by Collett Cox.

Jeffrey Hopkins was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1972). He served at the University of Virginia as Associate Professor and Director of the Center for South Asian Studies (1973–2005).

Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. After earning his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1993), he joined Rice University in 2002 as the J. Newton Rayzor Chair in Philosophy and Religious Thought and department chair.

Jeffrey Kotyk works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He earned degrees from Komazawa University and Leiden University (PhD 2017) and has held posts at McMaster University, the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman is a philosophy scholar who taught at Cornell (~1968–1974), Johns Hopkins (~1974–1980), and Boston University (~1984–2020), where he was University Professor and Professor of French Literature. He also held a post at Yale and various visiting professorships.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned his BA and PhD (~1970) at Harvard. His posts include Associate Editor at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (1981–1992).

Jeffrey Newmark specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (~1992–1996) and the University of British Columbia (~2003–2009), and held a post at the University of Winnipeg around 2011.

Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 2003) and Berry College.

Jeffrey Samuels specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2002) under Karen Christina Lang and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After earning his undergraduate degree at Brown and his PhD at Princeton University (~1976), he served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from UNC Wilmington, UT Knoxville, and UCLA (PhD attested 2013 under Gregory Schopen). He held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego (attested 2013).

Jenkuan Shih is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he was supervised by Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, after completing an MA supervised by Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

Jennifer Jung-Kim works in history/archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, including assistant director (attested 2016) and lecturer (attested 2026).

Jenny Hung is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She earned PhDs from HKUST (2013) and Lingnan University (2018), and serves as an Assistant Professor in the Division of Humanities at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.
